# Question Threshold Evidence If NO

Signed by Month 1; no casting vote; deadlock clocks (panel by day 10, partial suspension day 14, impaired confidence day 21/28); Go needs at least 4 of 5 criteria including detection and parity, and a straddling interval means Modify. Any gate slipping over 2 weeks triggers a summit within 5 days. Co-signed instrument text and an unclassified copy of the scoring rule, checked at Month 1 (Month 0.5 for the escalation roadmap). USD 625M per country (25%) deposited at Month 2, equal on both sides; access authority enacted; tranche delay of 14 days or less. A delay over 14 days goes to co-chair escalation, and over 30 days or unresolved unequal deposits is a Stop trigger. Treasury deposit records and the enacted statutes or equivalent, at Month 2. Each pair meets the functional-equivalence criteria (at least 500 sq m staging, 24-hour access, at least 50-ton lift, at least 2 maintenance events per month, all proposed). Co-chair certification of the reciprocal-access audit, signed Statements of Cooperation, locked parity definition and dry-run access timings, by Month 3 (dry-run confirmation Months 4.5-5). DOWNSIZE: exclude the asymmetric pair and fall back to 2 pairs (4 sites) at 4 exercises per site per month (48 total). Below 2 pairs, or if shielding is found, STOP.
4 Is the neutral facility certified and is the ledger, key custody and recovery chain proven? Facility of at least 1,000 sq m operational and hardened by Month 3; first dual-share key ceremony Month 4; recovery rehearsal Month 5 with key loss recovered within the estimated 24 hours; 1-hour digest exchange with 30-minute overdue alert; mismatch escalated within 4 hours; reconciliation target 72 hours. Host-country MOU (Month 1.5), hardening certificate (Month 3), ceremony and rehearsal records, ledger divergence drill results (Months 4-5). DELAY then DOWNSIZE: switch to the pre-staged backup host. If no certified facility exists by Month 5.5, re-scope or stop. Gate slips over 2 weeks escalate to a summit.
5 Is the pre-clock calibration passed and the entry gate certified? Evidence rule: false positives 7-13%, false negatives under 5% on a 100-200-event historical cohort (second cohort if deviation over 5 points). Pilot of all 7 event types done. At least 80% of staff certified by Month 5 and at least 6 positions per shift on at least 2 pairs. Unverifiable or excluded equipment at most 5% (over 10% at a site or overall is a Stop). Thresholds locked at Month 5.5. Calibration Confidence Memo, pilot report, certification roster, vendor-participation registry and unverifiable-share calculation, all at Month 5.5. DELAY or MODIFY SCOPE: a failed second cohort or staffing shortfall postpones the clock start under the gate-slip rules. Unverifiable equipment over 10% at a site or overall means re-scope or STOP. Fix the last viable start date, since the Month 9 backstop leaves no test.
6 Does the 90-day test score Go, Modify or Stop against the locked thresholds? 54 exercises (48 at 2 pairs) with at least 6 per event type. Detection at least 70% (planned class) and 50% (unplanned class), false positives at most 10%, unverifiable at most 5%, parity at least 85%, no discrepancy over 21 days, fewer than 5 open material cases, no hard Stop trigger. Go needs at least 4 of 5 including detection and parity. Modify is 3 of 5 or correctable weaknesses. Stop is 2 or fewer or any hard Stop. Independent scoring of exercises, ledger and parity dashboards, scored within 5 days after Month 9. Final decision by Month 9.5. A NO means Modify or Stop. Modify means rework or a later phase. Funding for it is OPEN, so tranche 4 use and the rework route must be decided before Month 8. Stop means shutdown, with success claimed only for monitored changes at participating declared sites.

1. Go test statistic and effective thresholds (🔴 High)

Decision: Which statistic is compared with each Go threshold (point estimate, or a lower confidence bound), and are the 70%/50% class thresholds kept or reset?

Why it is open: Verdict logic says Go needs intervals not straddling a threshold. With ±22% (planned) and ±25% (unplanned), Go needs about 92% and 75% detection (recomputed). Executive summary, review plan and self-audit use inconsistent examples and an unsupported 50-60% success estimate.

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Compare point estimates with thresholds; intervals reported but not gating. Go reachable at 70%/50% detection. Weaker statistical defensibility; contested verdict risk. verdict_logic; executive summary; review plan 5.3, 9.1; self-audit item 8.
B. Compare lower bound at a stated one-sided confidence level; state effective Go detection levels. Rigorous, but Go needs very high detection; most outcomes become Modify. verdict_logic; detection_thresholds; scoring rubric.
C. Reset class thresholds (proposed thresholds) so the interval rule is reachable. Keeps the straddle rule; changes the detection bar and needs revalidation at pre-registration. detection_thresholds; verdict_logic; KPI dashboard.
  • If nobody decides: The rule stays as written; Go is nearly unreachable, and tranche 1 is not released without a mechanical verdict rule.
  • Owner: Co-Chair Steering Board (double-key), via the bilateral instrument
  • Decide by: Month 1 (2026-11-08): the scoring rule must be locked in the instrument.
  • Blocks: Month 1 (2026-11-08) instrument signature, tranche 1 release (Month 2 = 2026-12-08), and the Go/Modify/Stop verdict.

3. Authority of external escalation body (🔴 High)

Decision: Does the external or neutral escalation authority only convene and report, or hold a delegated decision right limited to a pre-agreed fallback?

Why it is open: The review plan gives a third-country official a 48-hour summit, binding scope-reduction power and a voting chair, which conflicts with double-key governance and the canonical 5-day summit. The authority is appointed before the instrument that would grant its powers.

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Convene, monitor and report only; scope reduction is a pre-agreed mechanical double-key rule (e.g. fall back to 2 pairs). Preserves double-key; slower in deadlock. Review plan 3.1, 12.2, 12.3, 15.2; instrument.
B. Both co-chairs delegate in advance a decision right limited to the single fallback. Faster, with bounded neutral power; needs both legislatures' comfort. Instrument; governance matrix; review plan.
C. No external authority; co-chair summit only. Simplest; deadlock relies on automatic partial suspension. Remove authority from review plan and exec summary.
  • If nobody decides: Summit within 5 days, co-chairs only; the neutral authority is not appointed.
  • Owner: Both national co-chairs (double-key)
  • Decide by: Month 0.5 (2026-10-23), before any appointment, and in time for the Month 1 (2026-11-08) instrument.
  • Blocks: Month 1 (2026-11-08) instrument; gate-slip escalation procedure.

4. Mid-test access asymmetry rule (🔴 High)

Decision: What size and duration of access asymmetry is a hard Stop, is any cure period allowed, and is mid-clock site substitution permitted?

Why it is open: Constraints and review plan say asymmetry is an immediate Stop. The premortem and self-audit allow a 30-day cure at a gap over 10% and substitution within 48 hours, which breaks matched-set parity and exercise load.

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Immediate Stop on defined asymmetry; no substitution. Matches user constraint; fragile to operator delay; parity ≥85% scored. Premortem FM3; self-audit 20; hard_stop_triggers.
B. Short defined cure period, then Stop; no substitution. Tolerates fixable delays; the cure must be defined (threshold, days) and may cut exercises. Instrument; parity definition; deadlock clocks.
C. Allow substitution with a pre-clock-equivalent audit. Keeps pairs but resets the parity baseline and may drop to 48 or 36 exercises. exercise_load; site eligibility; schedule.
  • If nobody decides: Canonical text applies: access asymmetry is a Stop trigger, and conflicting documents are unresolved.
  • Owner: Co-Chair Steering Board
  • Decide by: Month 1 (2026-11-08): written into the instrument; parity locked before Month 3 (2027-01-08).
  • Blocks: Month 3 (2027-01-08) matched-pair approval; Phase One scoring.

Why it is open: The review plan states 8-12 specialists at USD 2-3M, funded from the personnel envelope, but elsewhere from free contingency. Recomputed cost of 16-24 specialists is about USD 1.3-1.9M per month, so USD 2-3M covers 1-2 months.

A. Use the existing 36-person surge pool inside the personnel envelope. No extra draw; may strain other surge needs. Review plan 3.3, 6.3; exec summary.
B. Free-contingency draw with a pre-authorised limit. Covers peaks; reduces the USD 400-450M free contingency. contingency_rules; instrument.

Focus and Context

Can a 90-day bilateral US–China operational test credibly verify declared frontier-computing equipment changes at matched datacenters using mirrored inspectorates, tamper-evident ledgers and reciprocal challenge exercises—or will thin statistics, governance gridlock and unvalidated procedures render the verdict politically contested and Phase One non-credible? The Consortium is a first-of-kind proof-of-concept at national-security scale with USD 5 billion committed. Success depends on locking thresholds, evidence rules and deadlock procedures before operations begin.

Purpose and Goals

Deliver a Go/Modify/Stop verdict on the feasibility of frontier-computing equipment-change verification between adversaries by Month 9.5 (2027-07-23), grounded in 54 blind-challenge exercises, dual-ledger synchronization and adjudication of disputed findings under equal co-chair governance. Success criteria: ≥70% detection of planned-event changes, ≤10% false positives, ≤5% unverifiable equipment, ≥85% reciprocal-access parity, <21-day max discrepancy age at conclusion, <5 open material cases. Verdict must be pre-registered mechanical outcome, not post-hoc political negotiation.

Key Deliverables and Outcomes

Bilateral instrument locking deadlock, suspension, evidence-weighting rules and the mechanical scoring method (Month 1 = 2026-11-08); numeric verdict thresholds locked at Month 5.5 (2027-03-23) after the pilot; validated confidential evidence rule (Calibration Confidence Memo, Month 5.5 = 2027-03-23); pilot exercise (all 7 event types, Month 5 = 2027-03-08); 54 Phase One exercises with independent scoring and published detection rates with confidence intervals (Months 6–9 = 2027-04-08 to 2027-07-08); Go/Modify/Stop verdict scored mechanically against locked thresholds within 5 days of Phase One conclusion (Month 9.2–9.5); ledger divergence reconciliation <72 hours (100% closure by Month 9 = 2027-07-08); adjudication panel recommendations on all contested findings (zero cases unresolved >28 days if possible).

Timeline and Budget

Entry conditions Months 0–5 (2026-10-08 to 2027-03-08.5); Phase One 90 days Months 6–9 (2027-04-08 to 2027-07-08); verdict by Month 9.5 (2027-07-23). Budget USD 5.0 billion (USD 2.5 billion per country), seven envelopes, four synchronized tranches, contingency USD 500M (10% of total; USD 50–100M compression reserve + USD 400–450M free contingency). Personnel cost ~USD 29M/month full strength; Phase One about USD 86–115M personnel; ramp-up cost pre-clock estimated USD 60–80M (TBD). Any entry gate slipping >2 weeks triggers an emergency co-chair summit within 5 days; an 8-week slip is estimated to cost USD 100–200M (20–40% of contingency; 22–50% of free contingency). Draws above the compression reserve require double-key approval; facility slips are funded from free contingency, not the reserve.

Risks and Mitigations

Entry-condition sequencing lacks binding acceleration; 8-week slip consumes an estimated USD 100–200M (20–40% of the 500M contingency), compresses Phase One from 90 to 50–60 days, widens statistical confidence from ±12% to ±18–20%, making Go/Modify/Stop verdict ambiguous. Mitigation: establish Entry-Condition Task Force with external escalation authority, parallel tracks, explicit scope-reduction power by Month 0.5 (2026-10-23). Evidence-weighting rule unvalidated against adversarial scenarios; false-positive rate could reach 15–20% (vs. 10% target), overloading adjudication capacity (15/month planned), aging discrepancies past automatic suspension thresholds (days 14, 21, 28) and cascading partial-site suspensions by Month 7 (2027-05-08). Mitigation: historical validation plus 20–30 synthetic adversarial test cases (Month 5 = 2027-03-08); pre-fund adjudication surge (8–12 specialists, USD 2–3M) by Month 4 (2027-02-08). Verdict thresholds remain provisional, inviting post-hoc renegotiation; a detection interval straddling a criterion threshold (e.g. 70% planned-class detection with about ±22% interval) could let either co-chair claim victory or fault. Mitigation: lock the mechanical scoring method (Go needs at least 4 of 5 criteria including detection and parity; Modify 3 of 5; Stop 2 or fewer; an interval straddling a threshold means Modify, per criterion at one confidence level) in the bilateral instrument by Month 1 (2026-11-08) and numeric thresholds by Month 5.5 (2027-03-23); publish unclassified logic before first exercise (Month 6 = 2027-04-08) so legislatures see objective procedure.

Audience Tailoring

Bilateral arms-control verification specialists and executive-decision makers (US and Chinese national co-chairs, oversight bodies, legislative appropriations committees). Technical rigor and precedent-grounded risk assessment prioritized over commercial or accessibility framing. Classified material referenced but not disclosed; unclassified summary paths specified.

Action Orientation

Establish Entry-Condition Task Force by Month 0 (2026-10-08) with binding weekly milestones, parallel-track activation (sites, vendors, inspectors), and external escalation authority. Appoint Independent Exercise Authority by Month 3 (2027-01-08) and locked evidence-rule specification in escrow by Month 4.5 (2027-02-23). Lock bilateral instrument with deadlock procedures and the mechanical scoring method by Month 1 (2026-11-08); lock numeric verdict thresholds by Month 5.5 (2027-03-23). Pre-position adjudication surge staff, neutral-facility hardening, and key-recovery rehearsal by Month 5 (2027-03-08). Certify entry gate by Month 5.5 (2027-03-23). Execute Phase One from Month 6 (2027-04-08) to Month 9 (2027-07-08), publish verdict within 5 days.

Overall Takeaway

The Consortium's Go/Modify/Stop verdict credibility depends entirely on pre-clock governance lock-down: bilateral instrument embedding deadlock and suspension rules, validated evidence-weighting rule (false-positive rate within ±3 points of 10% target), and mechanical verdict-scoring logic (Go needs at least 4 of 5 criteria including detection and parity; default to Modify when a confidence interval straddles a threshold). Entry-condition sequencing must run in parallel with external escalation authority and scope-reduction backstop (2 pairs over the full 90 days, 4 exercises per site per month = 48 total; a shortened clock falls below the minimum and cannot support Go) to prevent 8-week slips that exhaust contingency and degrade statistical confidence. If entry gates slip and adjudication capacity is under-resourced (5 specialists per country for 30–50 cases/month), the program stalls in automatic partial suspensions by Month 7 (2027-05-08) and reaches Stop by default due to operational failure, not evidence failure. Success probability 50–60% if entry gates lock by Month 5.5 (2027-03-23) without compression; drops to 20–30% if >4-week cumulative slip occurs.
